source: Minchat Shai on Exod 8:15 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi collated; the Masorah's two; the Ramah; Minchat Kohen; Shemot Rabbah 15; Rabbenu Bachya)
claim_en: va-yomru ha-CHARTUMIM ('and the MAGICIANS said: it is the finger of God'): the magician-word's whole file, with a FRONT-RANK DISCREPANCY. The Ramah's rule as MS quotes it: the construct form is lean-vav everywhere (three stations — Gen 41:8, Exod 7:11, 7:22, asserted); the long form is FULL with yod everywhere EXCEPT TWO ruled LEAN — the finger-verse HERE and the boils-verse (Minchat Kohen's mnemonic: 'lice, boils') — so the precise books, the Masorah's two-lean note, and the Ramah against the HILLELI's full. THE STREAM SPLITS THE PAIR: at the boils it is WITH the ruling (be-chartumam lean, Exod 9:11 — census checked, the form's only station) — but HERE it writes ha-chartumim FULL (asserted; the Masorah's lean skeleton standing ZERO times in the stream): SNAPSHOT with the Hilleli camp against MS's books, the second such Hilleli-siding since Genesis — DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION FILED, dual-track, never merged. The chain's readings on the lean tradition named: Rabbenu Bachya — 'until now full; at the plague where THEY COULD NOT, the yod fell out: their wisdom fell short'; Shemot Rabbah — the singular be-chartumam: 'their flesh above was struck first'; and the ten measures of sorcery, nine to Egypt.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 8:1 (the Masorah's pair; Pesachim 53b)
claim_en: ve-HAAL et ha-tzfardeim ('and BRING UP the frogs'): the bring-up imperative stands exactly TWICE in the Torah (census checked) — the frogs onto Egypt here, and 'and BRING THEM UP to Mount Hor' (Num 20:25 — AARON'S DEATH-ASCENT): the Kitzur carries the Pesachim chain whole — 'what did Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya see, that they gave themselves to the furnace? They reasoned a fortiori from the FROGS: the frogs gave themselves to death for the sanctification of the Name — and afterward ESCAPED, as it is written: the frogs died from the houses, the courtyards, and the fields (8:9) — but NOT from the OVENS; but Moses and Aaron, of whom it is said BECAUSE YOU DID NOT BELIEVE IN ME TO SANCTIFY ME — they died and did not enter the land': the Masorah's own pair binds the frogs' ascent to the ascent on which Aaron dies, and the chain reads the furnace of Daniel out of the space between them.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 8:12 (the Ramah's rule; Midrash Lekach Tov)
claim_en: ve-haya le-KHINIM ('and it shall become LICE'): written LEAN — 'this one ALONE lacks its yod, and every other lice-word in the Torah whose nun is read with chiriq is written full with yod' (the Ramah's rule; census checked: the lean form once, here — the full forms landing at 8:13 and 8:14 asserted, and the collective ha-kinam pair read with qamatz standing outside the rule, asserted): and the Lekach Tov reads the missing letter twice — 'lean, because the making of lice WAS WITHHELD from the magicians' knowledge more than the other plagues: the demon cannot create a creature smaller than a BARLEYCORN'; and again: 'all the dust was lice, and the magicians stood ON the lice with their feet never touching the earth — and a sorcerer whose feet do not touch the ground effects NOTHING: therefore, THEY COULD NOT' (8:14): the plague spelled one letter short exactly where the imitators' craft ran short.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 8:10 (the Ramah; the printer's margin corrected); Kitzur on 8:10
claim_en: chomarim CHOMARIM ('heaps upon heaps' — the dead frogs gathered): BOTH tokens written LEAN, no yod (census checked: the lean form exactly twice, both in this verse) — 'and the one of Behaalotcha (the quail: he who gathered LEAST gathered TEN HEAPS, Num 11:32) is FULL, as the Masorah there rules; Minchat Kohen brought it here, and the PRINTER here erred in the margin, making the second one full — and the Ramah transmits as we said' (the run's fourth printed-authority correction; the quail's full third asserted): the Kitzur completes the Masorah's three: 'even here, the one who gathered least gathered ten heaps' — the quail-rule read back into the frog-heaps: two plagues, one measuring-word, and the doubled lean pair heaped in one verse.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 8:19 (the Masorah's three)
claim_en: ve-samti FEDUT ('and I will set a DIVISION between My people and your people'): written LEAN — the redemption-word's ONLY Torah station, and the full skeleton standing zero times in the Torah (census checked); the Kitzur's Masorah-three: 'this one LEAN and two FULL — REDEMPTION He sent to His people (Ps 111:9) and WITH HIM is abundant REDEMPTION (Ps 130:7): for THIS was not a complete redemption, only from the swarms; but when they went out of Egypt it was complete — that is, redemption He SENT to His people; and in the future, abundant redemption — a complete deliverance': three spellings grading three redemptions — the partial one lean in Egypt, the complete one full at the going-out, the final one full and abundant: the word's letters keep the ledger of how much rescue each verse holds.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 8:9 (the Hilleli; the Masorah at Masei; the Ramah; Minchat Kohen)
claim_en: min ha-CHATZEROT ('from the COURTYARDS' — where the frogs died): written LEAN 'in the Hilleli copy and in the precise books — one of the FOUR lean in this form, the sign transmitted in the Masorah magna at the head of Masei, and so the Ramah and Minchat Kohen': the census verifies the Torah side — the lean form stands ONCE in the Torah, here, and the full skeleton ZERO times (checked; the list's other stations live beyond the Torah's stream, named by their Masei sign): the courtyards of the frog-deaths spelled one letter thin, with three authorities and the Masorah's own index-card concurring on the letter the stream carries.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 8:12 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: ve-HAKH et afar ha-aretz ('and STRIKE the dust of the earth'): the strike-imperative's ONLY Torah station (census checked) — its Scripture-twin Ezekiel's 'STRIKE palm to palm' (Ezek 21:19): the Kitzur — 'teaching that the lice STRUCK and clapped on their faces and on all their flesh' (the dust-plague hearing the palm-clap verse); and the plague's reason carried with it: 'because Egypt barred Israel from the BATHHOUSES, and through this their clothes filled with lice — therefore they were struck with LICE' (measure for measure, the bathhouse-ban repaid in vermin): one strike-word, the dust below and the clapping above.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 8:5 (the Masorah's three)
claim_en: u-le-AVADEKHA ('and for your SERVANTS — for when shall I entreat...?'): the and-for-your-servants form stands exactly TWICE in the Torah (census checked) — Moses' entreaty-offer here and the cattle-plea of Reuben and Gad ('and your servants have CATTLE,' Num 32:4), with Jeremiah's third named ('what have I sinned against you and against your servants...?' — spoken to Zedekiah FROM THE PIT, Jer 37:18): the Kitzur reads the three as the swarm... the frogs' reach: 'even had they hidden themselves UNDER THE GROUND (the pit-verse), there the frogs would come and destroy them; and they destroyed the yield of the field until no PASTURE remained for the cattle (the cattle-verse)': the entreaty-word's own concordance maps where the plague could go — underground and into the fodder.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 8:14 (the Masorah's three)
claim_en: ve-LO YAKHOLU ('and they COULD NOT' — the magicians against the lice): the Kitzur's Masorah-three read across Scripture — the rowers of Jonah's ship ('and the men dug in to return to the dry land, and COULD NOT,' Jonah 1:13) and Moab's king ('to break through to the king of Edom — and they COULD NOT,' 2 Kgs 3:26): 'teaching that even had they FLED TO THE SEA from the lice, there the lice would come against them and fight them' (the sea-verse read as the escape that fails; the in-verse token checked): the two-word confession of the craft's limit, heard by the chain as a door closing on every exit — and the finger-of-God confession stands one verse below it.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 8:13 + 8:20 (the presumed-readings lists)
claim_en: The PRESUMED-READINGS FESTIVAL: three stations of the sevirin class ('presumed' readings the Masorah guards against) in ONE chapter — kol afar ha-aretz ('ALL the dust of the earth,' 8:13): 'one of the list written KOL without vav where readers PRESUME ve-khol' (and-all; the bare form checked in-verse); u-VET avadav ('AND the house of his servants,' 8:20): 'one of the FOUR bet-and-bet where readers presume IN-the-house' (asserted); u-ve-KHOL eretz mitzrayim ('and IN all the land,' 8:20): 'one of the FIVE where they err, presuming ve-khol — the sign transmitted at Ezekiel 27 in the Masorah magna' (asserted): with the refusal-station of last chapter (le-shalach ha-am, 7:14) the corpus's presumed-readings file gains four Exodus stations in two chapters — at every one, the letter is leaner than the reading the ear expects, and the Masorah stands guard exactly there.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 8:4 (the Masorah's pair; Berachot 54b)
claim_en: ve-YIZBECHU la-YHWH ('THAT THEY MAY SACRIFICE to the LORD' — Pharaoh's own mouth, bargaining): the sacrifice-word here is the JUSSIVE — pointed with the plain vav of purpose, against the Torah's two PRETERITE and-they-sacrificed (the covenant-offerings 24:5, the calf 32:8 — the three-way pointing split asserted at the build; the in-verse jussive checked): the Kitzur's Masorah pairs it with the thanksgiving-psalm — 'and let them SACRIFICE sacrifices of thanksgiving' (Ps 107:22): 'FOUR must give thanks — and one of them, HE WHO GOES OUT OF THE PRISON' (Berachot's four brought whole): the first sacrifice-word Pharaoh ever grants is pointed as a wish, and the concordance hears in it the thank-offering of released prisoners.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 8:2/8:7/8:20 (the letter-and-accent file; Ibn Ezra; the Michlol)
claim_en: The chapter's letter-and-accent file: va-taal ha-TZFARDEA ('and the FROG came up,' 8:2) — 'the he WITHOUT the lengthener in the precise books, and the tzadi DAGESHED as I wrote at 7:27' — both halves on the stream's own letter (the no-lengthener asserted; the hard tzadi checked — EX07-01's one-singular rule landing at its own station in-span); ve-SARU ha-tzfardeim ('and the frogs shall TURN ASIDE,' 8:7) — accented MILRA, on the last syllable (Ibn Ezra and the Michlol folio 135; the mark's position on the stream's own accent asserted); u-mi-BATEKHA ('and from your houses,' the second, 8:7) — 'the bet with a גלגל (wheel-stroke)': the stream stores the token under its zaqef with no second mark — STATION ELEVEN of the wheel-class, and a NEW wrinkle honestly filed: a ruled word-internal second stroke the stream's one-mark-per-word field cannot carry (the class's gap deepens); and the pe of faro SOFT at the swarms' entry (8:20, asserted): the plague-chapter's marks, four rulings deep.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 8:1 (the no-break ruling); the send-wordplay anchored
claim_en: The remainder: THE SEND-WORDPLAY (8:17, anchored): im-enkha MESHALEACH et ami, hineni MASHLIACH bekha — 'if you are NOT SENDING My people, behold I am SETTING-LOOSE upon you the swarms': the refused send-verb turned causative weapon in one verse (both skeletons checked at the build — the letter answers the unsent people with unleashed vermin, the book's send-ledger writing its own irony); and the PARAGRAPH-SEAM ruling (MS on 8:1): 'in the precise manuscripts there is NO break between the frogs-shall-come-up (7:29) and AND-THE-LORD-SAID (8:1)' — Or Torah found so in a Rambam-descended manuscript and others, and so the Meiri — the warning and the execution written as ONE paragraph (the paragraph layer stands uninstrumented in the corpus — the standing gap class — the ruling filed named-only): the chapter that opens without a seam closes its file on a wordplay the stream spells exactly.
